attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The finite-dimensional Schur/cross-ratio derivation is valid, but it is not yet a Yang-Mills proof because the analytic boundary trace theorem for reflected Wilson collars is missing. We still need to prove that the actual continuum limit has either no multiplicative anomaly or only a rank-one anomaly after the locked individual renormalizations; equivalently, we need a real RG/OPE estimate showing all Wilson boundary log cross-ratios vanish.
steps: Start from regulated reflection positivity: for every fixed collar distance \(\delta>0\), the finite matrix \(S_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta W_i,T_\delta W_j)\) is positive semidefinite.

Use the RG-to-OS fixed-collar convergence hypothesis to pass \(a\downarrow0,L\uparrow\infty\), obtaining \(N^{(\delta)}\ge0\). This is the already valid closed-cone part, provided the topology controls reflected Wilson probes.

Take \(\delta\downarrow0\). Diagonal trace continuity and positive-contact Cauchy-Schwarz eliminate positive additive contacts, leaving the sharp obstruction in a multiplicative anomaly \(N=\Gamma\circ M\).

The intended OS matrix is therefore \(M=\Gamma^{[-1]}\circ N\). If \(\Gamma^{[-1]}\ge0\) as a finite kernel, the Schur product theorem gives \(M\ge0\) from \(N\ge0\). Conversely, if the bridge is supposed to work for arbitrary positive finite collar matrices, testing matrix units and two-by-two positive matrices forces \(\Gamma^{[-1]}\) to be positive.

Assume also that the boundary anomaly \(\Gamma\) is positive and diagonally normalized. For every pair, positivity of \(\Gamma\) gives \(|\Gamma_{ij}|\le1\); positivity of \(\Gamma^{[-1]}\) gives \(|1/\Gamma_{ij}|\le1\). Hence \(|\Gamma_{ij}|=1\). A positive matrix with all normalized entries of modulus one is rank-one, so \(\Gamma_{ij}=r_i\overline r_j\) up to phase, and in the positive real case \(\Gamma_{ij}=r_i r_j\).

Taking logarithms in the positive real case gives \(\log\Gamma_{ij}=\log r_i+\log r_j\), hence every log cross-ratio vanishes. Conversely, vanishing of all such cross-ratios reconstructs \(r_i\) from one reference row, proving rank-one diagonal congruence.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The argument proves a necessary and sufficient finite-matrix transfer criterion, not the required Yang-Mills estimate. It also uses a universal Schur-multiplier criterion stronger than positivity for one accidental family of actual matrices; to turn a nonrank-one anomaly into a concrete contradiction one must either realize a bad positive direction in the actual Wilson OS matrices or directly compute an actual target matrix with negative determinant.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: Wilson Boundary Cross-Ratio Test

assumptions: Fixed-collar reflected Wilson probes are valid test observables for the RG cutoff-removal topology: for each \(\delta>0\), \(S_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta W_i,T_\delta W_j)\to S(\Theta T_\delta W_i,T_\delta W_j)\).
For each fixed \(\delta>0\), reflection positivity holds before cutoff removal and therefore the fixed-collar continuum matrix \(N^{(\delta)}\) is positive semidefinite.
Diagonal trace continuity has been locked: \(S(\Theta T_\delta W_i,T_\delta W_i)\to S(\Theta W_i,W_i)\) after the permitted individual Wilson-loop renormalizations.
The remaining boundary trace defect is multiplicative and finite on the chosen family: \(N_{ij}=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}N^{(\delta)}_{ij}=\Gamma_{ij}M_{ij}\), with \(\Gamma_{ij}\ne0\).

Any additive positive boundary contact has zero diagonal after diagonal trace locking, hence vanishes by Cauchy-Schwarz; if an additive nonpositive contact remains, it is separately a falsifier of OS-compatible boundary OPE.

The extra rank-one conclusion assumes \(\Gamma\) is itself a positive boundary kernel, as would be expected if the anomaly is generated by an auxiliary reflection-positive boundary degree of freedom rather than by an indefinite subtraction.
definitions: source object: regulated and then continuum fixed-collar Schwinger matrices \(N^{(\delta)}_{ij}=S(\Theta T_\delta W_i,T_\delta W_j)\) obtained from reflection-positive lattice/RG Yang-Mills observables in the locked gauge-invariant algebra.

target object: intended OS-positive continuum Schwinger matrix \(M_{ij}=S(\Theta W_i,W_j)\) on the uncollared positive-time Wilson observables, prior to adding any boundary counterterm or changing Wilson-loop renormalization.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, now refined to the two-step passage fixed collar \(\delta>0\) followed by trace limit \(\delta\downarrow0\) for every finite reflected Wilson OS matrix.

same-theory condition: the collar trace may identify \(T_\delta W_i\to W_i\) only through the already chosen individual renormalizations of the locked observable algebra; a pair-dependent factor \(\Gamma_{ij}\) is allowed only if it is an invertible diagonal congruence already present in that algebra.

Schur reciprocal multiplier: for a nonzero matrix \(\Gamma\), \(\Gamma^{[-1]}\circ N\) must be positive semidefinite for every positive semidefinite finite matrix \(N\) arising at the interface; the universal finite-matrix version asks this for all \(N\ge0\).

log cross-ratio certificate: for positive real entries, \(K_{ijkl}=\log\Gamma_{ij}+\log\Gamma_{kl}-\log\Gamma_{il}-\log\Gamma_{kj}\); rank-one diagonal congruence is equivalent to \(K_{ijkl}=0\) for all indices.

equations.valid_when: Valid only after additive contacts have been excluded or shown to vanish and after individual Wilson-loop renormalizations have already been locked as part of the same theory.

equations.valid_when: This transfers positivity from every positive collar-limit matrix \(N\) to the intended target matrix \(M\) exactly when \(\Gamma^{[-1]}\) is a positive semidefinite kernel, by the Schur product theorem and its finite converse.

equations.valid_when: Valid as a universal finite-matrix falsifier showing that a normalized damping anomaly \(\beta<1\) cannot justify a theory-independent positivity bridge unless the actual Yang-Mills matrices avoid the bad positive direction for an additional reason.

equations.valid_when: Valid for strictly positive real anomaly entries; with phases the corresponding condition is that the normalized entries have modulus one and form a coboundary phase.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Compute \(K_{ijkl}\) for four reflected Wilson collar families. A nonzero value, or even a two-loop normalized damping \(0<\Gamma_{ij}/\sqrt{\Gamma_{ii}\Gamma_{jj}}<1\) together with an actual matrix direction \(t>\Gamma_{ij}\), is a concrete falsifier of the same-theory positivity bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates the finite-dimensional algebraic heart of the same-theory OS bridge. The closed-cone step proves \(N\ge0\); the lemma says exactly when a multiplicative Wilson boundary anomaly lets one infer \(M\ge0\) without changing the continuum theory.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let \(W_1,\ldots,W_n\) be a finite family in the locked positive-time gauge-invariant Wilson observable algebra, and let \(T_\delta W_i\) be mirror-compatible collar representatives supported at distance \(\delta>0\) from the reflection plane. Suppose fixed-collar RG convergence gives positive OS matrices \(N^{(\delta)}\) and the boundary trace limit has no additive contact term but may have a multiplicative anomaly \(\Gamma\): \(N_{ij}=\Gamma_{ij}M_{ij}\), where \(M_{ij}=S(\Theta W_i,W_j)\) is the intended target OS matrix. Then the collar positivity bridge is valid for arbitrary finite OS matrices exactly when \(\Gamma^{[-1]}=(1/\Gamma_{ij})\) is a positive Schur multiplier. If, in addition, \(\Gamma\) itself is an OS-positive boundary kernel with nonzero entries, this forces the normalized anomaly to be rank-one, equivalently all logarithmic four-point cross-ratios vanish. Thus any nonzero Wilson boundary log cross-ratio is a same-theory falsifier, not merely a removable normalization defect.

assumptions: The boundary anomaly admits an asymptotic logarithm after standard perimeter, cusp, and composite Wilson renormalizations are fixed individually.
The individual terms \(u_i+u_j\) are allowed only if they correspond to the preselected observable normalization; otherwise even a diagonal congruence is a bookkeeping change that must be declared.
The pair term \(B_{ij}\) is measured on a finite family of Wilson observables for which the fixed-collar OS matrices are already valid limits.
definitions: boundary pair interaction: the part \(B_{ij}\) of \(\log\Gamma_{ij}\) depending jointly on the reflected loop \(\Theta W_i\) and the positive-time loop \(W_j\), after subtracting all individual loop renormalizations.
rectangular second difference: \(\Delta B_{ik;jl}=B_{ij}+B_{kl}-B_{il}-B_{kj}\), equal to the log cross-ratio of \(\Gamma\).
Wilson hairpin test family: loops whose collars approach the reflection plane with controlled tangent, cusp angle, or small boundary segment, chosen to magnify pair-dependent collision effects.

equations.label: pair-interaction decomposition
equations.valid_when: Valid when the multiplicative anomaly is positive real and has a logarithmic expansion after individual counterterms are separated.

equations.label: cross-ratio equals pair second difference
equations.valid_when: Valid whenever all four anomaly entries are nonzero; individual terms cancel identically.

equations.label: model boundary exchange obstruction
equations.valid_when: Valid as a model for a boundary-local OPE/exchange defect; if the boundary kernel has rank greater than one, suitable boundary charges can make the cross-ratio nonzero.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find four Wilson collars with \(\langle \rho_i-\rho_k,G_{\partial}(\rho_j-\rho_l)\rangle\ne0\), or a perturbative cusp/hairpin term whose coefficient depends jointly on both loops. Such a nonzero second difference is a falsifier of rank-one same-theory transfer.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma translates a Yang-Mills analytic boundary calculation into the finite matrix criterion of Lemma 1. It gives a practical way to search for a falsifier: compute only the rectangular second difference of the mixed boundary anomaly, because all individual renormalizations cancel.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the logarithm of the mixed Wilson boundary anomaly decomposes as \(\log\Gamma_{ij}=u_i+u_j+B_{ij}\), then the diagonal part \(u_i+u_j\) is only an individual congruence, while the pair interaction \(B_{ij}\) is harmless exactly when all its rectangular second differences vanish. A cusp, hairpin, or boundary exchange term producing a nonzero rectangular second difference yields a nonrank-one anomaly and therefore a Schur-transfer falsifier unless compensated by an already locked observable identification.

assumptions: The contact term is a finite Hermitian matrix on every finite Wilson family.
The contact term is positive semidefinite if interpreted as an independent boundary reflection-positive contribution.
Diagonal trace continuity gives \(A_{ii}=0\) after subtracting the multiplicative diagonal normalization.
definitions: additive contact matrix: a possible boundary term in \(N_{ij}=\Gamma_{ij}M_{ij}+A_{ij}\) supported by the collision of \(\Theta T_\delta W_i\) and \(T_\delta W_j\) at the reflection plane.
diagonal trace continuity: the condition that the diagonal entries have the same collar and target limits after the locked individual renormalizations.
positive boundary contact: an additive contact form that is itself reflection-positive on finite Wilson families.

equations.label: Cauchy-Schwarz contact kill
equations.valid_when: Valid for every finite positive semidefinite contact matrix.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If an explicit boundary OPE calculation gives \(A_{ii}=0\) but \(A_{ij}\ne0\), then either \(A\) is not positive or diagonal trace continuity was falsely asserted; in both cases the OS bridge has a genuine falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This removes one apparent loophole: a positive additive mixed contact cannot hide off diagonal once diagonal trace continuity is locked.
candidate_lemmas.statement: After diagonal trace continuity is established, any remaining additive boundary contact matrix \(A\) compatible with reflection positivity must vanish: if \(A\ge0\) and \(A_{ii}=0\) for every observable in the finite family, then \(A_{ij}=0\) for all \(i,j\). Therefore the only surviving mixed boundary obstruction is either an indefinite additive contact, which directly violates OS-compatible boundary OPE, or a multiplicative nonrank-one anomaly detected by the log cross-ratio.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from this bridge if a perturbative or constructive Wilson hairpin/cusp calculation produces a stable nonzero log cross-ratio after all permitted individual renormalizations are removed.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the bridge if one proves for a dense mirror-smooth Wilson core that additive contacts vanish and all multiplicative boundary anomalies have zero log cross-ratio, with RG convergence valid for the corresponding reflected probes.
control_decision.reason: The branch has moved from an abstract closed-cone topology to a concrete finite Wilson matrix invariant. This is high learning because it supplies both a proof target and an explicit falsifier: compute the boundary log cross-ratio.

dependency_updates.description: The formal closed-cone part remains valid for fixed collars, but the bridge now needs a finite Schur multiplier/no-cross-ratio theorem for the boundary trace of Wilson OS matrices.

The observable algebra must be locked before the trace limit. Individual diagonal congruences may be harmless only if already part of that locked algebra; pair-dependent anomalies are same-theory failures.
The topology must control not only each reflected pairing but also the limiting multiplicative cross-ratios of four mixed Wilson pairings near the reflection plane.

falsifiers: falsifier: a four-loop reflected Wilson collar calculation with nonzero \(K_{ik;jl}=\log(\Gamma_{ij}\Gamma_{kl}/\Gamma_{il}\Gamma_{kj})\), showing a pair-dependent boundary anomaly not absorbable as individual Wilson renormalization.
falsifier: a two-loop normalized damping anomaly \(0<\beta<1\) together with an actual collar-limit off diagonal \(t\) satisfying \(\beta<t<1\), giving \(\det M=1-(t/\beta)^2<0\).
falsifier: a boundary cusp or hairpin anomalous dimension depending jointly on both loops at the reflection plane rather than as a sum of one-loop terms.
falsifier: an additive boundary contact with zero diagonal and nonzero off diagonal, which cannot be a positive contact and therefore contradicts OS-compatible trace continuity.

falsifier: an attempted proof that absorbs \(\Gamma_{ij}\) by changing the Wilson-loop algebra after cutoff removal; that may yield a positive modified theory but not a valid same-theory OS bridge for Yang-Mills.
falsifier: RG compactness estimates that converge on separated collars but fail to control the four-entry cross-ratio limit as collars approach the reflection plane.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 186 converts the Wilson boundary obstruction into a computable invariant: the logarithmic cross-ratio of the multiplicative anomaly. The finite-dimensional theorem is valid and sharp: collar positivity transfers to the intended OS matrix through a multiplicative boundary defect exactly by a reciprocal Schur multiplier, and under a positive boundary-kernel hypothesis this leaves only rank-one diagonal congruences. Therefore the remaining Yang-Mills problem can be attacked by calculating or bounding \(K_{ik;jl}\) for reflected Wilson collars; a nonzero value is a same-theory falsifier, while \(K=0\) on a dense Wilson core would strongly promote the OS bridge.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the one-loop or heat-kernel model boundary collision of four mirror-smooth rectangular Wilson collars approaching \(t=0\); extract \(\Gamma_{ij}\), subtract individual perimeter/cusp terms, and test whether \(K_{ik;jl}=0\) or yields a concrete mixed Wilson falsifier.
